chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad and a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, all of them from Al-Washa', who said:

I heard Al-Rida (peace be upon him) saying: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'May God curse whoever kills someone other than his (intended) killer, or strikes someone other than the one who struck him.'

And the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'May God curse whoever initiates an unlawful incident, or shelters the initiator of one.' I said: 'And what is the initiator?' He said: 'The one who kills.'

key_terms.آوَى مُحْدِثاً: Shelters an initiator — harboring or protecting a criminal from justice
key_terms.أَحْدَثَ حَدَثاً: Initiates an unlawful incident — to cause/begin a crime, here clarified as killing
key_terms.الْمُحْدِثُ: The initiator — defined here as the killer, the one who starts the chain of violence
key_terms.قَاتِلِهِ: His intended killer — the specific aggressor who actually attacked him
key_terms.لَعَنَ اللَّهُ: May God curse — a prophetic formula of divine condemnation

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet say about killing someone other than your attacker in al-Kafi?
ai.summary: This hadith transmits two prophetic curses on those who transgress the principle of proportionate retaliation in disputes. The first forbids retaliatory killing or striking against anyone other than the actual aggressor; the second extends the curse to those who begin unlawful violence (the muhditth, here clarified as the killer) and to those who shelter such perpetrators. In early Islamic legal culture, this teaching addressed the tribal custom of collective blood vengeance, where an entire clan might suffer for one member's act — the Prophet's words aimed to confine retaliation strictly to the individual culpable party.
